invariants: A clean Windows checkout resolves only versioned and pinned inputs before replacing a release.
Publishing consumes the exact archive produced by a successful reusable verification job.
open_questions: Review rc.1 provider/consumer changes and obtain new acceptance; alpha observations cannot certify this revision.
identity: Candidate Git commit and pinned reference SHA identify the gate; frontend bytes are separately pinned prebuilt inputs.
ownership: Verification owns build directory, dependency environment and reports. Publish job consumes uploaded archive and never rebuilds it.
ordering: Resolve runtime, locked dependencies and frontend manifest before replacing dist; build, full pytest, upstream consumer tests, raw Cordis oracle, scoped acceptance, isolated boot, then artifact upload.
errors: Missing or changed inputs fail before overwriting the previous distribution; any test/runner failure blocks archive publication. C58 raw exit 1 is accepted only by the exact-signature gate.
cancellation: Interrupted validation produces no success summary or verified archive for publication.
adaptation: Current Windows/Python 3.8.10 gate. Frontend is the exact checked-in build, not a fresh target-source rebuild; Web Connection batch owns source/protocol alignment. Win7 is deferred.

rc1_review.scope: The revised executable corpus and current Source inputs define bounded acceptance; historical alpha reviews remain historical.
